topics.topic: Definition, contents, ownership, trust, retention, and recovery handling of the retention-action record
questions: What named record holds these decisions, which identifiers and outcomes must it contain, who maintains it, and what happens when it is missing, incomplete or unavailable after a restore?
What system or document is the owner's record, what facts and identifiers must it retain so actions can be repeated, who maintains it, and which trust and retention rules apply to it?

quotes:
What the
owner repeats after a restore — erasures, restrictions, ends of a
relationship — follows the owner's own record of the retention review
(R0-60).

The periods —
the owner's provisional ones of R0-40 among them, to be checked against
accounting, tax, claim and building-warranty periods — are the governance's
retention schedule, applied by the owner's periodic review (once a year, say).

The owner first starts the restored instance owner-only (A17 rule 1), so
   no service and no agent reaches it, and brings each Customer and project to
   the state the owner's own record of the retention review (R0-60) gives for
   it now — erased, restricted, ended or not — and erases audit entries before
   the latest date the owner erased by, before configuring the tokens and
   starting it again.

This is the owner's operation (Explicit exclusions: the
   host's administration), and the owner's record is its evidence; Registry,
   which no longer holds those changes, cannot list them, enforce them or
   tell when this is done. Its guarantee after a restore is what the backup
   held.
judgement.divergence: One implementation requires a durable owner-maintained recovery ledger keyed by Customer and project identifiers with every retention outcome and audit cutoff, and refuses recovery completion when it is unavailable; another relies on informal notes or memory and starts services despite missing decisions. The owner, services, agents and affected customers notice whether erased, restricted or ended states are correctly restored.
judgement.why: Recovery depends on an external record, but the texts do not name it, define its required facts, establish its trust and retention rules, or say what happens when it cannot support replay.

topics.topic: Where retained migration materials are stored, how they are protected, and how they are disposed of after backup
questions: What named system or medium holds these materials, who can access it, and what protection applies while it contains production personal data?
After a checked backup contains the import, must the retained export and import choices be securely deleted, archived under a stated retention rule, or left at the owner’s discretion?

Where are the export, project picks, replacement names and aliases kept, who can access them, how are they protected, and what observable disposal action occurs when a checked backup holds the import?

quotes:
A store lost before a checked backup holds the import
loses the import with it, and the import may then be made again: the owner
keeps the export file and the picks, names and aliases given in the import
until a checked backup holds the import, and retires the VPS instance only
then (R0-79).

The owner makes the export of a source with a one-time migration script run on
the source's host. The script is not a Registry operation: production Registry
gains no export action, and the source keeps none after the migration. What
Registry defines is the file it accepts on import; its format belongs to States
5 and 6.

The uploaded file is kept in the owner session that uploaded it, never in
   the store, until the import is accepted, another file is uploaded in that
   session, or the session ends (M11); then it is dropped.

An accepted import drops the
   file of the session that confirmed it; a file another session keeps stays
   until that session ends, and its confirmation is refused because the
   import is closed (rule 8).

| `personal_data` | Project display name (R0-82); Object address, kind and characteristics (R0-38); Customer name, phone, e-mail, language, tax id, legal name (R0-80); the import file uploaded in an owner session (M11), which holds such values |
judgement.divergence: One implementation keeps an access-controlled, encrypted external recovery copy and securely deletes it when a checked backup contains the import; another keeps the materials on an unspecified medium indefinitely or deletes them without an observable confirmation. The owner and privacy or recovery operators notice the difference during disposal, access review or a pre-backup restore.
judgement.why: The later rules dispose of Registry's session copy, but neither they nor State 0 identify or govern the separate materials R0-89 requires the owner to retain.
judgement.failure: the quoted passage of a consequential gap is not found verbatim in the texts

topics.topic: Whether retained migration materials are a temporary governed exception to the one-home rule
questions: Is the retained migration export a temporary exception to the one-home rule, and if so, what exact period and governance record authorize that exception?
Is this retained export and import record an explicit temporary exception to the one-home rule, and must it be listed in the governance until removed?

quotes:
A store lost before a checked backup holds the import
loses the import with it, and the import may then be made again: the owner
keeps the export file and the picks, names and aliases given in the import
until a checked backup holds the import, and retires the VPS instance only
then (R0-79).

A customer's living personal data — name, contact data, tax id (NIF/NIE/CIF),
legal name — and the object's address and identifying characteristics are held
only by Registry, as the target R0-81 sets for the other services. Other services
keep no customer record and no copy of these values; they read them by
`customer_ref` or project id when they use them.

Client Portal's offline projection (R0-39) is Portal's publication to the customer:
it holds only what the customer's own cabinet shows, never a tax id, and is the
one kept copy this rule admits besides issued documents.

Registry is the one home of a customer's personal data and of the object's
address and identifying characteristics: the platform's target is that no other
service keeps a customer record or a copy of these values, except as fixed in a
document it issued and in Client Portal's offline projection (R0-80). Copies
that remain until each service removes them are listed in the governance
(R0-81).

Until each has, the governance's records of processing list
the copies that remain, with their service and the change that removes them.
judgement.divergence: One implementation treats the retained migration materials as a governed temporary copy, records their location and removal condition, and removes them when a checked backup holds the import; another treats the owner's copy as outside the one-home rule and leaves it unlisted or retained. The owner and governance or privacy reviewers notice the different inventory and disposal state.
judgement.why: The one-home rule is framed as a transition and therefore does not contradict R0-89, but the texts do not decide whether this owner-held copy is governed like the listed service copies or what must happen to it after its stated minimum retention period.

topics.topic: Whether restoration replay includes all inverse and related retention actions
questions: Is that list exhaustive, or must the owner also replay inverse or related retention actions lost after the backup, such as lifting restrictions, resuming relationships, project anonymisations and audit-entry erasures?
